instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(B)(3) requires itemized reporting of meal/food/beverage expenditures only once cumulative payments to a particular official during the calendar year exceed $50, establishing a $50 itemization de minimis threshold.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: Ohio's lobbyist registration trigger (§101.72) is based on engagement to actively advocate, not on a compensation dollar threshold. The statute defines "legislative agent" in §101.70(F) by whether actively advocating is "one of the individual's main purposes," with no dollar amount specified.

Ohio's registration requirement (§101.72(A)) is triggered by engagement of a legislative agent within ten days, not by any expenditure dollar threshold. No expenditure-based registration trigger appears in the statute.

The statute requires statements to report total expenditures regardless of amount (§101.73(B)(1), (C)); there is no overall dollar threshold below which filing is excused. Only the $50 meals itemization threshold exists, which is captured in the itemization row.
No time-percent de minimis threshold for filing appears in §§101.70–101.79; filing obligations attach to all registered legislative agents and employers without a percent-of-time exemption.
